  <item rdf:about="https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/730150817">
    <title>Pleistos (River)</title>
    <link>https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/730150817</link>
    <description>A river in Central Greece that rises near modern Arachova in Boetia. It flows west through a karst valley paralleling the Gulf of Corinth, often underground, hence one modern name (Xeropotami). Augmented by streams issuing from Mount Parnassus, the river passes the site of ancient Delphi, which overlooks the valley from the north side. Thereafter the river bed follows elevation gradients, turning south as it passes the location of modern Hrisso to enter the Gulf of Corinth on the eastern edge of the modern village of Kirra. Extensive, long-term olive irrigation and other landscape change, have likely altered the river's course throughout history. Another modern drainage, arising in the Amphissa valley to the northwest and entering the Gulf of Corinth further west, is also today labeled as the Pleistos, but this seems to be a modern application of the name.</description>

  <item rdf:about="https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/573571">
    <title>Tripodiskos</title>
    <link>https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/573571</link>
    <description>Now unlocated, Tripodiskos was a market center of Megara. According to Pausanias, its name is connected to the activities of Coroebus who was ordered by the Pythia of Delphi to carry the Delphic tripod and to establish a new shrine to the god at the place where it fell from his hands. This was Tripodiskos; Pausanias indicates that Coroebus' tomb was located in its agora.</description>
